findings.body: Because Array.prototype.forEach ignores the promise returned by its async callback, any rejection from getCalendar/deleteEvent becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of being caught by the surrounding try/catch, so the error is never logged via logger.error and the outer function returns before the calendar/meeting cancellation has actually completed.
findings.failure_mode: Asynchronous errors bypass the enclosing try/catch and resolve after the function has already returned, causing silent failures and out-of-order cleanup.
findings.impact: Because Array.prototype.forEach ignores the promise returned by its async callback, any rejection from getCalendar/deleteEvent becomes an unhandled promise rejection instead of being caught by the surrounding try/catch, so the error is never logged via logger.error and the outer function returns before the calendar/meeting cancellation has actually completed.
findings.root_cause: An async function was passed to Array.prototype.forEach, whose returned Promise is not awaited by forEach.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => {...})` with `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => {...}))` inside the try block so rejections are awaited and caught.
findings.title: forEach(async) callback breaks try/catch and skips awaiting calendar cancellation
findings.trigger: Rescheduling a booking whose bookingRefsFiltered contains a `_calendar` reference where the newly-async `getCalendar(...)` call throws or rejects (e.g. malformed credential type, failed dynamic app import) or `calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` rejects.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch at line 125 changes `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach((bookingRef) =>` to `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) =>`. The async callback's returned promise is ignored by forEach, so rejections from `await getCalendar()` or `calendar?.deleteEvent()` bypass the surrounding try/catch at line 124. The function proceeds to sendRequestRescheduleEmail at line 143 without awaiting completion.

raw_findings.body: forEach does not await the async callback, so (a) any rejection from getCalendar/deleteEvent becomes an unhandled promise rejection with no error handling at all in this code path, and (b) the subsequent `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` call executes without waiting for calendar/video cancellation to finish, creating a race where the reschedule email may be sent before the old event is actually removed.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unawaited async work executes out of order relative to subsequent logic and unhandled rejections are not surfaced.
raw_findings.impact: forEach does not await the async callback, so (a) any rejection from getCalendar/deleteEvent becomes an unhandled promise rejection with no error handling at all in this code path, and (b) the subsequent `sendRequestRescheduleEmail` call executes without waiting for calendar/video cancellation to finish, creating a race where the reschedule email may be sent before the old event is actually removed.
raw_findings.root_cause: An async function was passed to Array.prototype.forEach, whose returned Promise is neither awaited nor error-handled.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Await the cancellations before proceeding, e.g. `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => {...}))` prior to calling sendRequestRescheduleEmail, and wrap in a try/catch to log failures.
raw_findings.title: forEach(async) callback causes unhandled rejections and a race with sendRequestRescheduleEmail
raw_findings.trigger: Rescheduling a booking with a `_calendar` reference where the newly-async `getCalendar(...)` call throws/rejects, or simply where calendar/meeting cancellation takes non-trivial time.

raw_findings.body: Each credential's getCalendar (which performs a dynamic app import) is awaited before starting the next iteration, increasing total cancellation latency compared to resolving them concurrently.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Increased end-to-end latency for booking cancellation when multiple calendar credentials exist.
raw_findings.impact: Each credential's getCalendar (which performs a dynamic app import) is awaited before starting the next iteration, increasing total cancellation latency compared to resolving them concurrently.
raw_findings.root_cause: A for...of loop with await was introduced to sequence async getCalendar calls where they could be run concurrently.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use `await Promise.all(calendarCredentials.map(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); apiDeletes.push(...); }))` to resolve calendars concurrently.
raw_findings.title: Sequential await in for...of loop serializes calendar resolution that was previously synchronous
raw_findings.trigger: A booking whose user has multiple `_calendar` credentials (calendarCredentials.length > 1) needing cancellation via the legacy code path (no credentialId on the booking calendar reference).

finding.title: Sequential await in for...of loop serializes calendar resolution that was previously synchronous
finding.trigger: A booking whose user has multiple `_calendar` credentials (calendarCredentials.length > 1) needing cancellation via the legacy code path (no credentialId on the booking calendar reference).
finding.verifier_reason: Patch replaces `.forEach((credential) => { const calendar = getCalendar(credential); ... })` with `for...of` loop using `await getCalendar(credential)` at lines 480-483. This serializes previously-parallel synchronous calls. With multiple calendar credentials, latency increases. The impact is real but low severity as claimed.
